about.title: Corcoran Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Corcoran residents rely on a limited number of local clinics and hospitals, and many also travel outside Kings County for specialized care in Fresno, Bakersfield, or Visalia. When something goes wrong during that care — a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, a medication mix-up — patients are often left confused about whether what happened was simply a bad outcome or something more. California law recognizes that not every poor result is malpractice; a claim generally requires showing a provider failed to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that the failure caused harm. Because these cases hinge on medical records, expert review, and strict filing deadlines, getting an early read from someone familiar with how these claims work matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we're a free connection service that matches Corcoran residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate the specifics of what occurred, explain your options, and take the case on contingency if they move forward with you.

whyChoose.title: What Corcoran Patients Should Know About These Claims

items.title: Strict Filing Windows Apply
items.desc: California generally gives patients one year from discovering the injury and no more than three years from when it occurred to file, so waiting to sort things out can cost you the right to pursue a claim at all.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider must typically receive 90 days' advance notice, which affects how and when a case gets built.

items.title: Expert Medical Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, California cases almost always need a qualified medical expert to confirm the standard of care was breached — something an experienced attorney knows how to arrange.

items.question: I had a bad result from surgery in Corcoran — does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and that this failure caused your harm, not just that the outcome was disappointing. An attorney can review your records to help determine whether the standard of care was met.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after discovering a medical error?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discover (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth having your timeline reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes — California law caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages like medical costs and lost income are generally handled separately and aren't subject to that same cap.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney in Corcoran?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
